text: People Share DraftKings reduces workforce as company embraces AI DraftKings is undergoing a restructuring, according to various LinkedIn posts from now-former employees, who were unexpectedly laid off. By Erik Gibbs - 24 Feb, 2026 More about the author DraftKings is undergoing restructuring in some areas of the organisation, according to various LinkedIn posts from the now-former employees, who were unexpectedly laid off from the company. Several individuals from different business segments, including software engineering and recruitment, have confirmed that they were laid off unexpectedly and are now looking for other job opportunities. A DraftKings spokesperson told NEXT.io : “DraftKings has decided to reorganise some teams to better align their people with the most important priorities and areas of investment for the company. “Unfortunately, these changes will impact some roles across the organisation. The company believes that while these decisions are difficult, they are necessary to best position them for future growth.” It is worth noting that on the careers section of its website, DraftKings continues to list 80 open roles at the company. The layoffs came soon after the operator’s co-founder and CEO, Jason Robins, announced DraftKings’ strong performance in 2025. In the announcement, he stated that the company closed the year with its fourth-quarter revenue increasing by 43% year-on-year, marking record revenue and adjusted EBITDA, while the business is off to a strong start in 2026. The sentiment among investors remained negative despite the optimism, with DraftKings shares declining significantly since September 2025. They began that month at around $47.91, but have fallen significantly to around $21.81 as of 24 February. In a note sent to investors, analyst Jordan Bender of Citizens estimated the headcount reduction could approach 5% of employees. Based on a median employee salary of roughly $100,000, he projected potential annual cost savings of around $30m. He also indicated the timing, roughly 10 days after earnings and forward guidance, suggests the savings were likely incorporated into 2026 EBITDA guidance of $700m-$900m. DraftKings focusing on prediction markets and AI The restructuring follows the December launch of DraftKings Predictions , the company’s prediction market platform. Management is moving infrastructure to Railbird as its primary exchange as it prepares for major sporting events, including March Madness, the World Cup and the upcoming 2026 NFL season. The impetus behind these operational changes appears linked to intensifying competition in event-based markets. A more detailed strategic roadmap is expected at the company’s investor day on 2 March. Artificial intelligence (AI) is also central to the company’s evolving cost structure. Over the past two years, management discussions have frequently referenced enterprise-wide AI implementation. On the internal front, as Bender emphasised, DraftKings uses AI to automate requests for proposals, aid its engineers with coding, and implement chatbots and preliminary legal opinions. The purpose of these tasks is to minimise outsourced labour. On the external front, customer engagement and promotional strategies increasingly feature AI. Currently, about 70% of promotional spending decisions are made by AI models, and this trend is set to rise. The company regards this as part of its approach to personalisation and promotional efficiency. Bender suggests further rationalisation of operating costs may follow as markets mature and automation expands. While cost savings may support margins, additional workforce reductions remain possible as the company continues aligning expenses with strategic priorities. Share
